Note test: `I.subtract([[0, 4]], (4, 9)) == [(0, 3)]` — hole from 4 to 9, removes 4..9, leaves 0..3. Yes.

`subtract([[5,7],[1,3]], (2,6))` → normalize to [(1,3),(5,7)]; hole (2,6): (1,3) → (1,1); (5,7) → (7,7). Result [(1,1),(7,7)]. Good.

Implement in-place file.

merge: sort by lo, then merge. For gap semantics: merge when next.lo - prev.hi - 1 <= gap. Test: merge([[10,12],[0,1],[5,6]], 3): sorted [(0,1),(5,6),(10,12)]; gap between (0,1) and (5,6) = 5-1-1=3 <=3 merge → (0,6); next (10,12): 10-6-1=3 <=3 merge → (0,12). Good.

Also merge should not require gap>=0. Fine.

Let me write the implementation.
